graph.summary: imatinib → BCR/ABL fusion protein → cell population proliferation → Chronic myeloid leukemia

evidence.snippet: Imatinib mesylate was the first representative BCR-ABL1 tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) class for the treatment of chronic myeloid leukemia.
evidence.explanation: Imatinib is a BCR-ABL1 tyrosine kinase inhibitor, i.e. it decreases the activity of the BCR-ABL fusion kinase.

evidence.snippet: This alteration gives rise to the BCR::ABL1 fusion oncogene, whose constitutive tyrosine kinase activity promotes uncontrolled proliferation and survival of leukemic cells.
evidence.explanation: The constitutive tyrosine kinase activity of the BCR-ABL fusion promotes uncontrolled proliferation of leukemic cells.

evidence.snippet: Chronic myeloid leukemia (CML) is a myeloproliferative malignancy marked through the excessive proliferative growth of functional myeloid cells.
evidence.explanation: Excessive proliferative growth of myeloid cells is the defining manifestation of CML.
